pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae Ia q.30 a.2, sed contra (quoting 1 John 5:7 and Augustine, De Trin. VII)
pairs.question: Tres sunt qui testimonium dant in caelo, Pater, Verbum et Spiritus Sanctus. Quid tres?
pairs.derivation: Genuine interrogative 'Quid tres?' explicitly asked and answered: source reads 'Quaerentibus autem, Quid tres? respondetur, Tres personae'. Dropped the framing speech tags 'Quaerentibus autem' (narrates the asking) and 'respondetur' (narrates the answering). Included the preceding scriptural sentence 'Tres sunt qui testimonium dant in caelo, Pater, Verbum et Spiritus Sanctus' as verbatim setup so 'tres' has a referent. Answer cut at the first full stop; what follows ('ut Augustinus dicit, in VII De Trin.') is an attribution tag, not part of the answer.

pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae Ia q.30 a.4, sed contra (quoting Augustine, De Trin. VII)
pairs.question: Quid tres?
pairs.derivation: Source reads 'cum quaereretur, Quid tres? responsum est, Tres Personae; quia commune est eis id quod est persona.' Genuine interrogative explicitly asked ('cum quaereretur') and answered ('responsum est'); dropped those two framing tags. Answer cut at the first full stop before 'quia commune est eis...', which is Aquinas's gloss elaborating, not the reported answer itself.
